title: Clarinetists: Wooden Joe, Dutrey, George Boyd; society bands versus rough bands
summary: He heard Sam Dutre at the roof garden, praises rough George Boyd, and distinguishes the nice society bands from the rougher dance bands.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: We were talking about clarinet players.
To Nicholas too, he was all right, Nicholas. I was, oh Joe Nicholas. Yeah he used to play clarinet too, Wooden Joe. But I played with him several times.
Do you remember hearing Sam Dutre play at all?
I heard him play on the roof garden with the Superior Band.
That before Big Eye played with him?

Yeah, before Big Eye. And I heard him play somewhere else, I can't think of it now, but he used to play mostly with Sam Morgan I believe. Yeah, he played with Sam Morgan. Because that's what I tell you, this rough kind of playing, that was George A. Boyd, I believe he was the roughest one and didn't know nothing about no music and could play the sweet clarinet. He was a big fella, kind of ugly, but he could play a clarinet. And he played with different good bands. All of them was good, but I mean at that time people wanted the jazz, like I say. If you'd do the nicer you'd play, well that was society. You'd play around here at the Frans Ami Hall for the society people because they had the society people at that time and they had the bad people, the ratty people at that time. Well all the nice balls and all that, well they'd hire all them nice bands. That was like Sam Morgan and Superior and all like that, Olympia and all like that. Them kind of bands that hired them, them kind of bands because they wasn't, you know, no ratty. But them other bands for them balls, them the band and the views. But for nice dancers like them people down there one time, them Frans Ami Hall and right here, this Copper Raiders, that was a door, that was a terrible band there. They used to come down here, I used to sit on this same step down there.
